transcript.text:
A dryer that “won’t stop” is often not a failed part straight away. Automatic/sensor programmes can keep extending if airflow is poor or the clothes are still being sensed as damp; an anti-crease setting may also continue intermittently after the drying part has finished. If it runs endlessly even on a short timed cycle, the timer/control or moisture-sensing circuit becomes more likely. 1. Switch it off and unplug it. Clean the lint filter thoroughly. If it is a condenser or heat-pump dryer, clean the accessible condenser/second filter as the manual allows; if it is vented, check the hose is not crushed or blocked. Restricted airflow makes drying take far longer.
2. Check the programme and options: try a short timed cycle with anti-crease/crease-care switched off. A timed cycle should finish at roughly the selected time.
3. Avoid testing with an overloaded drum or one very bulky item, as these can remain damp and prolong an automatic programme. Does it keep running on a timed programme too, or only on an automatic/sensor programme? And is an anti-crease/crease-care option selected?
it finishes and says End but then the drum keeps turning every couple of mins. not sure if anti-crease is on, i dont know what that is

That sounds like the normal anti-crease function, not a dryer that has failed to stop. After displaying End, many dryers briefly turn the drum every few minutes to prevent the laundry settling into creases. It usually continues until you open the door or until its post-cycle period finishes. 1. When it shows End, open the door. The occasional turning should stop; this is the usual way to end anti-crease.
2. Check that it is not still producing heat after End. Brief drum movement without heat is normal. Stop using it and arrange repair if the drum turns with the door open, or if it continues heating after End. Otherwise, no repair is needed.

candidates: Sensor programme being extended by restricted airflow or dampness sensing (medium)
Fault in the timer, moisture sensor or control electronics (low)
